author: reek
body: A text field must give back what was typed into it. That is the whole identity, it needs no external oracle, and nothing in the tree had ever asked for it. Four chapters cite UI chapter TextField -- AddressBar, Browser, DiffusionApp and TrackerApp -- and not one of them calls a single function from it, so every function compiled and none was run.

author: reek
body: Keys are typed as the code points of a real Text, read out with char-code, because that is what a key identity IS: KeyInput settles the contract, a character is its CCE code point and an editing key is a named constant above two to the twentieth.

author: reek
body: The ascii line is kept as the boundary statement. Feeding the ASCII numbers for H and i inserts two characters that are not H and i, because the field reads a key as CCE, and a caller that hands it ASCII gets plausible text that is silently wrong.

author: reek
body: The unfocused line is the control. A field nobody focused must still be empty after the same keys, so a run where every line came back populated would be reporting a dispatch that ignores focus.

author: reek
body: The cursor is read into a Text the moment each key lands. TextFieldState is updated with __record-set, which stores into the field and returns the SAME record, so a binding made before a later edit is not a snapshot of the state before it -- reading home's cursor after end had been pressed reported the end position, which is the aliasing contract and not a navigation defect.
